title: Kingdom
description: A sprawling kingdom of crumbling stone and rigid tradition at the centre of the known world, divided into cantrevs and stretching from the snowbound north to the storm-battered east. It is a land of vast, lonely coach roads between isolated settlements, where the Capital's reach thins with every mile. Its throne has stood empty since the royal court was killed, and a Regency governs in the crown's name while stern religious orders and ambitious upstarts carve out domains of their own. The Kingdom runs on inertia and largely ignores the rot taking hold in its forgotten corners, the Estate on its eastern coast foremost among them.
summary: The old kingdom at the centre of the world, held in regency since its court was killed, a land of lonely coach roads and provincial stagnation.

title: The Crossroads
description: A meeting of five roads on open ground, a day's ride from the Estate. Hired coachmen will not take the Old Road, so passengers are set down here to wait for the Caretaker. Cold fire-pits, a broken bench and abandoned luggage mark the waiting. The signpost at the centre carries five boards, one for each road, reading Guilt, Loathing, Failure, Regret and Disgrace. Travellers leave coins and small offerings at its base, as people still do at crossroads everywhere.
summary: A meeting of five roads where the Caretaker's coach collects those bound for the Estate; a place between places.

title: St. Martha's Reformatory
description: A grim stone structure perched on a desolate hillside. Its gray walls bear the weathering of harsh seasons, while inside, dormitories lined with iron-framed beds house troubled girls under the stern watch of the Sisters. The branding chamber remains most disturbing, its implements for 'marking the impure' surrounded by stains no amount of scrubbing can remove. Daily routines of prayer, labor, and harsh correction continue in this isolated place where the outside world's judgments cannot reach.
summary: A grim stone structure on a desolate hillside, serving as an isolated institution for troubled girls, known for its strict routines and branding chamber.

title: Woodsman's Cottage
description: A blackened foundation ringed by scorched trees, all that remains of the humble home where the Woodsman and his wife briefly gave shelter to the Runaway. The stone hearth stands amid the devastation, reaching skyward like an accusing finger. Despite years passing, no vegetation reclaims this scarred earth.
summary: A blackened foundation and scorched trees, all that remains of the humble home where the Woodsman and his wife once lived.

title: The Foetor
description: The broad farmland at the heart of the Kingdom, rolling fields of wheat and barley, orchards, and green hillsides dotted with sheep and goats. Its people named it the Foetor themselves, after the muck they spread on the fields every spring, and say it with a grin. The villages are small and close-knit, the whole region turns out together to bring in each harvest, and a traveller is rarely turned away from a farmhouse table.
summary: The Kingdom's rolling central farmland, cheerfully nicknamed by its own farmers for the muck on its fields.

title: Harvest House
description: A three-story farmhouse standing proudly among fertile fields, recently expanded as its owners' fortunes have risen. Though still modest compared to true noble estates, the newly-titled Lord and Lady have adorned it with hasty attempts at grandeur. Farm tools and practical implements have been replaced with imitation finery. Local farmers speak of invitations to dine with their former equals, though many note the curious pattern of travelers who never complete their journey to these celebrated feasts.
summary: A three-story farmhouse among fertile fields, expanded by its newly-titled owners, known for grand feasts and disappearing travelers.

title: Servants' Quarter
description: The farmhouse's ground floor, hastily converted from family living space to servants' quarters and food preparation areas. Livestock pens adjoin the kitchen, allowing the Carver immediate access to fresh meat. A sturdy cart with iron wheels stands near the back door, its bed stained dark despite frequent scrubbing. Servants hired from neighboring farms whisper about the master's insistence that all visitors be announced before being allowed upstairs, and the strange sounds that echo through the floorboards during late-night feasts.
summary: The ground floor of Harvest House, converted into servants' quarters and food preparation areas, with adjoining livestock pens and unusual practices.

title: Dining Hall
description: Once the farmhouse's modest common room, now expanded by knocking down walls to create space for a long table surrounded by mismatched chairs acquired from across the region. Candles in tarnished holders provide inadequate light, casting most of the room in shadow while illuminating the heaping platters that never seem to empty. The newly-installed sideboard sags under silver serving dishes that gleam with recent polishing, a stark contrast to the rough-hewn beams overhead where hooks meant for curing meats now hold tapestries awkwardly cut to fit the space.
summary: An expanded dining hall in Harvest House, featuring a long table for feasts, mismatched chairs, and heaping, never-ending platters.

title: Nursery
description: The uppermost floor, once sleeping quarters for a large farming family, now converted into an unsettling nursery despite no announcement of an expected child. The central cradle, built from butcher's blocks joined together, dominates the room with its unusual size and sturdiness. Walls once whitewashed now display crude paintings of feasting scenes, while strings of preserved meats hang from ceiling hooks in place of traditional mobiles. The Lady is often found here, rocking in a chair beside the empty cradle, her swollen form suggesting either impending motherhood or simply the effects of endless consumption.
summary: The uppermost floor of Harvest House, converted into an unsettling nursery with a large cradle made of butcher's blocks and crude feasting paintings.

title: The Duck Pond
description: A small farm pond ringed with reeds and shaded by a leaning willow, its bank trampled to mud where the sheep and goats come down to drink. A flock of ducks lives on it, and a boy from the farm sits on a flat stone at the water's edge to feed them. Beside the pond, a weathered soldier's banner still stands on its pole, bearing the Bastion.
summary: A small reed-ringed farm pond full of ducks, with an old soldier's banner standing beside it.

title: The Bottoms
description: The low country of the Kingdom's southeast coast, old marsh drained and held dry behind earth dykes, sluice gates and pumping mills. Its fields lie flat to the horizon below the level of the sea, with reedbeds and mudflats beyond the dykes, where a broad river splits into mouths on its way to the water. The Bottomers who dig, mend and man the dykes are a conquered people, keeping the sea off land they do not own. Though it has been Kingdom land for many generations, the Bottoms has never been declared a cantrev. Fevers rise from the damp in the warm months.
summary: The Kingdom's drained southeastern lowlands, held dry below sea level by the dykes its conquered people keep.

title: Lowhaven
description: The Kingdom's busiest port, where the river meets the sea. Cranes stand along its quays, and short railways run from the docks to the warehouses and out across the fields, lines the crown has long meant to carry up the coast and inland. The Crownlander quarter and its great church of the Light sit on the one ridge of high ground, an old dune line. Below it, in the low streets that flood first, the Bottomers who work the port leave small offerings to the Loa at the street corners.
summary: The Kingdom's busiest port, its cranes and rail yards worked by Bottomers who live in the streets that flood first.

title: The Sluice
description: An ancient network of brick culverts, cisterns and drainage tunnels beneath the Bottoms, far older than the dykes above and long since obsolete. Only its entrances have been mapped, and only roughly, and it runs inland further than anyone has followed it. Diggers raising new dykes break into it so often that most just curse, brick the hole back up and dig around it. Lately, a few swear they have heard squealing on the other side.
summary: Forgotten ancient waterworks beneath the Bottoms, unmapped beyond their entrances.

title: Stillbourne House
description: A great winged house of pale stone in one of the Kingdom's northern cantrevs, perfectly symmetrical, with a columned portico beneath a broad pediment and formal gardens stepping down to a river. Inside, its marble floors are polished bright, and the spotless rooms show little trace of life, save the family's portraits, hung in symmetrical rows along every wall, many of them painted very young.
summary: A pale, symmetrical winged house in the Kingdom's north, its gardens stepping down to a river.

title: The Hedge Maze
description: A hedge maze in the gardens of Stillbourne House, entered beneath an ornate stone arch, with dragons trimmed from the hedge standing guard at its turns. Flowers brought from abroad bloom along its walls. Only its outer paths are still open; the inner hedges have been left to grow together into a solid mass, sealing off its centre.
summary: A hedge maze of topiary dragons and exotic flowers, its centre sealed off by overgrown hedges.

title: The Capital
description: The Kingdom's capital, an old walled city of grey stone above a river, reached across a long bridge lined with statues of saints and scholars. Behind its walls rise the spire of its cathedral, the towers of old colleges and the dome of the Museum, and on the highest ground stands the palace, from which the Regency now governs.
summary: The Kingdom's old walled capital above a river, seat of the Regency.

title: The Sprawl
description: The crowded districts where most of the Capital's people live, packed inside the old walls and spilling out far beyond them. Crooked cobbled lanes wind between tall, narrow-windowed houses of stone and dark timber, built so close that their upper floors lean toward one another across the street.
summary: The Capital's crowded residential districts of crooked lanes and leaning houses, long since spilled past the walls.

title: The Brownstone
description: A tall, narrow house of soot-greyed brownstone and dark timber wedged among the leaning houses of the Sprawl, home and study to a scholar of the University. A tower rises at one corner under a steep spire, set with a round window whose leading forms a ring open at the bottom, with five spokes through it, and stone steps climb to an arched door. Its red roof tiles have begun to slip, and small barred windows at the foot of its walls look out from the cellar onto the street.
summary: A tall, narrow scholar's house with a spired tower, wedged among the houses of the Sprawl.

title: The Parlour
description: The Brownstone's ground-floor parlour, warm and well appointed, with deep chairs drawn up to the hearth. Over the mantel hangs a handsome portrait of the Ancestor, and in the corner stands a mechanical music machine of black wood and brass, its great horn rising from the figure of a mermaid. A tall cabinet beside it holds whiskey and a deep red wine, its bottles stamped with the Crimson Seal.
summary: The Brownstone's comfortable ground-floor parlour, with the Ancestor's portrait over the hearth and a brass music machine.

title: The Study
description: The Brownstone's first-floor study, where a tall writing desk overflows with scrolls, letters and maps, among them a sheet of calculations smeared with dried blood. Shelves of rare and forbidden volumes line the walls, a worn high-backed chair with strange markings scratched into its arms faces the hearth, and on the mantel ticks a clock with twelve spokes in place of numerals. A potted plant on the windowsill is kept carefully watered.
summary: The Brownstone's cluttered first-floor study of scrolls, forbidden books and a spoke-faced clock.

title: The Attic
description: The attic beneath the Brownstone's steep roof, lit by a single dormer, where a former student of the University lived while he worked here. An easel holds an unfinished painting of black shapes in a red blaze. In the corner stands a jointed training mannequin, run through with a dozen blades though the wood around them is unmarked. A veil embroidered with a single eye is drawn over its face. His narrow bed and scattered clothes are still where he left them.
summary: The Brownstone's attic, left as its last lodger left it, with an unfinished painting and a blade-pierced mannequin.

title: The Tower Room
description: The small round room at the top of the Brownstone's tower, lit through its five-spoked window. Its shelves hold a clay figure of a human torso twisted into ribbed and curling shapes, cold to the touch, and a many-sided stone that floats a finger's width above its base, glowing a colour no one has a name for. The room is arranged around a low stone altar, carved with the words: 'The sacrifice of fire is the gate to ruin.'
summary: The Brownstone's round tower room of strange relics, arranged around an inscribed stone altar.

title: The Cellar
description: The Brownstone's cellar, reached through a bolted hatch pasted over with papers and occult signs. Its shelves are stacked with tinned food. An iron cage holds a mass of flesh that heals as fast as it is cut, and in a chair bolted to the floor sits a man whose opened skull is driven full of iron nails, his body showing no sign of decay. In the corner, a starved, long-fingered thing is chained to the wall, a heart-shaped padlock on its collar.
summary: The Brownstone's bolted cellar, where its scholars keep their crudest and cruellest experiments.

title: The University
description: The Kingdom's ancient university, a cluster of old stone colleges around cloistered courtyards, approached up a broad flight of steps. Its learning is handed down rather than questioned. In steep wooden lecture theatres, aged professors read from their lecterns while rows of students copy down what they are told, and anyone who argues back is laughed out of the hall.
summary: The Kingdom's ancient, tradition-bound university, a cluster of stone colleges where professors lecture and students are taught not to question.

title: The University Library
description: A tall Gothic hall standing among the University's colleges, entered beneath a square tower, its long wings lit by rows of pointed windows. Inside, shelves climb to the vaulted ceiling, reached by wheeled ladders. The oldest books are chained to their shelves, and its occult texts are kept in a locked room below, open only to senior scholars.
summary: The University's great Gothic library, its oldest books chained to the shelves and its occult texts locked away below.

title: The Museum
description: A great domed hall of pale stone, holding the collected curiosities of centuries: antiquities, relics and oddities from every corner of the world, many of them bought from explorers who carried them home. Fossil skeletons tower over its central rotunda, and its galleries open onto wings of statuary, old armour and cases of pinned specimens. Lamps often burn late in its offices, where its curators work through the night.
summary: The Kingdom's great museum, a domed hall of antiquities, fossils and curiosities gathered from across the world.

title: The Conveyance Guild Hall
description: The Conveyance Guild's hall in the Capital, a great covered yard of coach sheds, stables and storehouses. Spare wheels are stacked along every wall, smiths fit coaches with iron plating and shutters, and crates of freight wait by the gates for every road in the Kingdom. Above the gate is painted its motto, 'Fair prices, in good times and bad', and the fares chalked on the board beneath it change far more often.
summary: The Conveyance Guild's great coaching yard in the Capital, full of wheels, armoured coaches and waiting freight.

title: The Crossed Swords
description: A tavern beside the Conveyance Guild's yard, under a sign of two crossed swords. Old coach lanterns, harness and wheel-rims hang on its walls, and it keeps the best whiskey on the coach roads. The drivers drink at the front, and the Guild's real business is done at the back, in the curtained booth where the Wagon-Master holds court.
summary: The drivers' tavern by the Capital's coaching yards, where the Conveyance Guild does its real business over whiskey.

title: The Catacombs
description: A maze of tombs and burial niches cut into the rock beneath the Capital, where the Kingdom lays to rest those it wants remembered: generals, poets and old families, generation upon generation, many sealed in with their arms and heirlooms. The deepest galleries were cut before the city was founded, and the names on their tombs have worn past reading. By old custom, mourners leave a pinch of salt at the threshold of every tomb, to keep the dead at rest.
summary: The tombs beneath the Capital, where the Kingdom buries its honoured dead and mourners leave salt to keep them at rest.

title: The Barracks
description: The army's barracks against the Capital's northern wall, a walled compound of long stone halls, storehouses and stables around a packed-earth drill yard. Recruits train there from dawn among rows of battered wooden training dummies, and wagons of supplies leave its gate each week for the keeps in the north. The Bastion hangs over the entrance, and the yard is kept swept and squared to the Drillmaster's standard.
summary: The army's walled barracks in the Capital, where recruits are trained and supplies sent north.

title: The Palace
description: The royal palace on the Capital's highest ground, a rambling mass of grey stone towers, spires and courtyards built up over centuries around the oldest walls in the city. Its long galleries and state rooms were made for a court of hundreds, and there are no longer servants enough to keep them, so whole wings stand shuttered with their furniture under dust sheets. The clerks and messengers of the Regency hurry through halls built for courtiers.
summary: The royal palace on the Capital's highest ground, half shuttered, now the seat of the Regency.

title: The Throne Room
description: The palace's throne room, a long hall whose walls are hung with the banners of the Kingdom's cantrevs. At its far end, on a raised dais, stands an old oak throne built over a rough, plain block of stone, on which every monarch of the Kingdom has been crowned. The throne sits empty, and the Regent holds his audiences standing beside it.
summary: The palace's banner-hung throne room, its empty throne built over an ancient coronation stone.

title: The Feasting Hall
description: The palace's great feasting hall, long and high-roofed, with a minstrels' gallery at one end and tables enough to seat the whole court. The court was killed here at a feast, and though the floor has been scrubbed and the tables stripped, the hall has not been used since. Rumour blames the shadowy Uncrowned Order, so extra sconces and candelabra have been brought in, and each nightfall a servant who does not linger lights every one of them, until no shadow is left anywhere in the hall.
summary: The palace's disused feasting hall where the court was killed, lit against every shadow each night.

title: The Regent's Office
description: The Regency's working office, set up in a plain wing once kept for the palace stewards rather than in any of the state rooms. At long tables, clerks copy out proclamations, curfews and bounties for riders to carry to every inn in the Kingdom, and a great map of the cantrevs covers one wall, stuck thick with pins. Behind the Regent's own desk stands a locked cabinet of things the Regency has seen fit to confiscate.
summary: The Regency's working office in a plain wing of the palace, where proclamations go out to every inn in the Kingdom.

title: The Tangle
description: A primeval forest across the Kingdom's north, below the high tundra, its trees so old and close that their roots knot together over the ground and little light reaches the forest floor. It rains often, and the paths are deep in mud. The army is garrisoned here to turn back the refugees coming south from Ostvengr, and its keeps stand among the trees, linked by trenches and barricades of sharpened stakes. Spiders den in the hollows of the deep wood, some grown large enough to take a man.
summary: A primeval northern forest of knotted roots and mud, where the army's keeps and trenches hold the border against Ostvengr's refugees.

title: The General's Keep
description: The largest of the army's keeps scattered throughout the north, a squat fortress of grey stone in a clearing cut from the trees, ringed by ditches and stake palisades. It was raised generations ago against Ostvengr, the Kingdom's most dangerous neighbour, and most of the army is still garrisoned along the border, though since the Fall its soldiers mostly turn back refugees. Banners of the Bastion hang from its walls, chaplains hold services in its chapel, and the lamp in the General's window seldom goes out before dawn.
summary: The army's main keep in the Tangle, raised against Ostvengr and now turning back its refugees.

title: The Outriders' Lodge
description: The Outriders' Union's lodge, a long hall of dark timber and fieldstone deep in the woods, reached by no road at all. Its roof is green with moss, cloaks and bedrolls hang drying along its porch, and smoke rises from the cookfires in the yard, where stables and rows of canvas tents spill out among the trees. Inside, a map room charts the Union's secret trails beside every coach road in the Kingdom, routes the Conveyance Guild would dearly like to find.
summary: The Outriders' Union's timber lodge deep in the woods, reached only by its own trails.

title: Cold Spring Glen
description: A narrow wooded valley climbing toward the high country, where a spring rises from the rock at its head, cold enough to ache the teeth. A small village of woodcutters and trappers lines the stream below it, the last settlement on the road north, and its single inn does a steady trade with the soldiers garrisoned further down. On a platform above the village hang great war horns, kept through the long wars with Ostvengr to warn the keeps below should an army ever come over the Mountain's shoulder.
summary: A narrow wooded valley below the high country, home to the last village on the road north and its war horns.

title: The Tundra
description: The high country at the foot of the Mountain, which keeps much of it in shadow through the afternoons. Snow lies on it most of the year, its dark pines thin out as the ground climbs toward bare rock, and the wind wails through its canyons. It is thought to be empty, and few have reason to go and see.
summary: Snowbound high country of pines and canyons in the Mountain's shadow, believed empty.

title: The Mountain
description: A lone peak rising from the tundra at the Kingdom's northern edge, far taller than any mountain of the range beyond the river. Its upper slopes are locked in ice and its summit is lost in cloud. Storms come down off it without warning, and the wind and cold turn back nearly everyone who tries to climb it.
summary: A lone, ice-locked peak rising from the tundra, far taller than any mountain beyond the river.

title: The Caliginous Cathedral
description: A deep cave high on the Mountain, which the cultists who worship there call the Caliginous Cathedral. Crude effigies of the Iron Crown, built from piled stone, bone and rope, stand among columns of ice, and the floor is scrawled with chalk circles and crusted with black wax. On the far wall they have carved a great ziggurat, which they say will rise here in truth when the Crown finds its king.
summary: A cave high on the Mountain where Iron Crown cultists worship among crude effigies, calling it a cathedral.

title: The Valley
description: A small, quiet valley in the Kingdom's south, near the Pelagian border, with a brook running down its length. Great old oaks and beeches stand along its slopes, and every autumn they cover the ground in leaves. Where the road leaves the valley, it crosses the brook by a small stone bridge, and on the far side the wind blows harsher.
summary: A small, quiet valley in the Kingdom's south, its brook crossed by a stone bridge on the road out.

title: The House on the Borderlands
description: A rambling old house of dark stone and timber by the bridge at the Valley's end, all steep gables and tall chimneys. Most of its windows are boarded, but lamps burn behind the rest at every hour, and above its door, the tracery of a pointed window forms a circle of five spokes. Inside, the walls are covered in the calculations of an unfinished Body of Work, and a cellar door is kept bolted.
summary: A rambling, half-boarded house by the Valley's bridge, its lamps lit at every hour and its walls covered in calculations.

title: The Shroud
description: The Kingdom's northeastern coast, a stretch of fishing villages built out over the water on piers, jetties and stilts. Sea fog rolls in most mornings, which is how the locals came to call it the Shroud, and the air always smells of salt and fish. Its people live by the boats and the nets, and they are as superstitious about the sea as fishing folk anywhere.
summary: The Kingdom's foggy northeastern coast, a stretch of fishing villages on piers and stilts.

title: The Sacred Pier
description: The oldest pier on the Shroud, reaching far out over deep water, where the fishing villages bless their boats before each season. Its posts are hung with charms, old nets and the figureheads of lost ships, and fishermen drop a coin from its end before every voyage.
summary: The Shroud's oldest pier, where fishing villages bless their boats and leave offerings to the sea.
